boundary_note: Bounded first pass for all five frozen records in Middle Tennessee Operations [February-April 1863]. Preserve per-engagement dates: Dover February 3, Thompson's Station March 5, Vaught's Hill March 20, Brentwood March 25 and Franklin April 10, 1863. The live NPS campaign heading does not replace any battle interval. Opening personnel and exact effective command boundaries remain unresolved. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads Infantry brigade [US]; I Cavalry Corps [CS]; the live field reads zero. Cist gives Coburn nearly three thousand and Van Dorn 10,000; Jordan and Pryor give Forrest some 2,000 and the Federal column five infantry regiments, some 600 cavalry and a battery.
claims.rationale: Column and corps figures from interested retrospective histories; no matched opening strength is adopted. Live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 2,206 total (US 1,906; CS 300); the live NPS field reads 1957 total (US 1600; CS 357;). Cist gives Coburn 40 killed, 150 wounded and 2,200 prisoners including the wounded, and the Confederates 35 killed and 140 wounded; Jordan and Pryor give Confederate losses of about thirty killed and 125 wounded.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Prisoners dominate the Union figure and are not an opening strength.

open_questions: Coburn's, Van Dorn's and Forrest's reports, returns and the escaped column's size remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Cist is an interested retrospective Union staff history; Jordan and Pryor is a retrospective Confederate history for most of whose statements Forrest's prefatory note accepts responsibility, and is not independent of Forrest. Where both are used they are separate families. Reports and newspapers cited inside either book are not additional families.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
